answer: Admission can be a one-shot observational exam, not a reusable profile. A registrar releases a short-lived flight of falcon beacons over a test range; each applicant records timestamps, signal strengths, and multipath errors in a sealed vault log, then presents an onyx-stamped transcript signed with its own key. Graders treat identical fade curves, matching clock skew, or the same missed-beacon pattern as one operator. Because the beacons are randomized and expire in minutes, a farm cannot replay one capture across many addresses without being clustered and barred from voting for two epochs.
